content.thinking:
I'm planning out the qilin's design in detail - a deer-horse quadruped body with a dragon head, antlers, cloud-swirl mane, scaled texture, cloven hooves, and an ox tail with a cloud tuft, all accented with gold trim and glowing eyes.

Working through the skeleton hierarchy now: a root hip joint connecting to spine, neck, head and jaw chains, plus separate tail and leg chains. I'm calculating specific joint heights and segment lengths for the hind and front legs so the IK bends naturally at the stifle/hock and elbow/knee, making sure the total limb length reaches from hip or shoulder down to the hoof.

For the body itself, I'm routing the spine as a curved path from hips to chest, with the neck curving up and forward into the head joint, then placing the head and jaw as sub-parts oriented along that final neck direction.

Naming the three neck joints with tapering radii, then adding the head joint parented to the neck tip with its own forward direction. For head geometry I'm setting up skull and snout shapes using local forward/up coordinates relative to the head joint.

Now I'm adding the lower jaw joint, positioned and aimed relative to the head, with its own frustum-box bone, plus teeth, fangs, flowing whisker sweeps, and a beard tuft under the chin. For the eyes, I'm placing anime-style eye decals onto the skull surface using local offset coordinates.

Still designing antler geometry...

Now I'm planning the ears as flattened fin-shaped extrusions on the head sides, and sketching a mane made of cloud-like scattered cards along the neck and chest with a white-teal swirl texture.

Continuing to figure out scatter placement: mane cards concentrated on the upper/back neck using normal filters, with wisp accents added at leg joints and fetlocks using frame sweeps along the leg geometry.

For the cloud puff SVG, I'm designing a layered-circle cloud shape with a swirl stroke -- flat white fill with a light teal shaded ellipse and ink-blue outline, drawn in greyscale so it can be tinted per-instance via a color option.

Drawing the cloud path and swirl details...

For body paint, I'm checking that a scales-based coat built through cel-shaded lighting resolves correctly as a layered Paint.

Deciding on the final palette: jade-teal scales with deeper teal edges, cream-gold belly, white-cyan mane, gold antlers and hooves, with magenta flame tufts as accent details, all composed through a countershade-then-cel pipeline for the body coat.

For the feet, I'm sketching cloven hooves as paired half-cylinders split slightly apart at the foot tip, positioned along the leg chain's endpoint joint to give a split-hoof silhouette rather than a single blocky foot.

Still working out the leg sweep radii, tapering each leg from thicker at the top to thinner at the fetlock, with coloring using the cel-shaded coat gradient toward a darker gold tone.

Then I'm layering on shoulder and haunch spheres to fill out the chest/hip silhouette, and starting to plan the tail as a chain running back from the hips.

Building the tail chain geometry...

Adding gold cuffs...

I'm placing gold swirl decals on the body flanks and shoulders at different z-positions, then adding glowing iris details, dark nostril spheres, and sweeping gold ridge spikes for the brows.

Now I'm sketching chin whiskers as cream-gold catmull-rom curves flaring from the muzzle, plus cheek fin extrusions. For teeth, I'm looping to place small spike shapes along the upper and lower jaw bones, with larger fangs mixed in.

Still defining helper logic... making sure limb chains, hoof joints, and part counts stay within limits.

Now I'm working out the spine and limb attachment points: shoulders parent to the spine's third joint while hind legs parent to the hips, with side-based naming for left/right. I'm placing hooves and shoulder joints at specific forward/backward offsets to get a natural standing pose, then checking leg length distances from hip to foot for the hind limbs.

Checking bend directions for front versus hind legs to get a deer-like elbow-back, knee-forward silhouette, then stacking up the body proportions from spine to belly, back, neck, head, and antlers to confirm the overall height lands around 2.3m, which feels right for a large qilin.

Now I'm working out the body loft, extending the sweep from the hips to form the rump and shaping the cross-section radius so the belly reads deeper than the back.

I'm connecting the neck to the chest cap and checking the neck-to-skull joint alignment, then tapering the neck radius profile along its length. I'm also scattering mane cards along the neck tube using a density and minimum-distance filter, aiming them backward and downward with a texture set for variation.

Now I'm adding smaller cloud wisps along the back and chest, plus elbow tufts at the leg joints, and setting up glow orbs for the antler tips and forehead gem.

I'm positioning the forehead gem relative to the skull's slight forward tilt and starting the antler construction function, computing base points from the head's local coordinates then offsetting outward in model space.

Working out the antler curve points and sweeping a beam along them with a flat start and pointed tip, using a gold/cream color for the material, then setting up tines branching off the main beam at a few points along its length.

Still defining whisker curves...

Now I'm thinking through a beard tuft under the chin, using a handful of flame-like card frames along the lower jaw bone with slight lean and flow variation for a natural hanging look.

For the cheek frills, I'm sketching a dragon-fin-like outline with sharp points and checking that the edges don't self-intersect.

Positioning it at the head with offsets for left, forward, and up, and working out the thickness direction so it's not parallel to the fin's plane. For coloring, I'm planning gold cel shading with teal accents, skipping separate ears since the fins serve that role, and setting up the skull's scale texture along with the snout's paint.

Still working out jaw geometry...

I'm setting up the jaw joint attached to the head with its aim point toward the snout tip, giving it a "jaw" role. I'm keeping color count under the 64 limit, skipping optional details like mane flames and dewclaws, and considering small wisp cards for fetlock tufts placed partway along the leg sweep near the elbow and hock.

Now I'm defining ring attachments for leg tufts, using ring items generated from the leg chain at points 0.9 (pastern) and 0.4 (knee) with varying counts and textures per leg.

Gold cuffs need placement too—I'm checking radius interpolation along the leg to avoid clashing with the tuft rings, settling on a cuff radius near 0.052 swept with a thin tube. Then I'm starting on spine spikes distributed along the body using the along() helper to place scaled spike shapes.

Now I'm drafting an SVG spiral decal for the flank, using curved gold strokes to form swirling cloud-like shapes.

I'm planning to layer a darker outline beneath the gold paths for contrast, then thinking through how to position and mirror the decal on each side of the body using a function that takes position, direction, and size, flipping it for the opposite flank.

I'm also working out the spine curve points along the body, adjusting the knot coordinates near the hips, mid-back, and shoulders to get a smooth catmull-rom path through the torso.

Now I'm defining the belly radius shift to lower it slightly, and setting up the tail chain starting near the hips with three segments curving down and back, with tuft cards placed along the tail's path.

I'm adding flame-colored tuft rings at the tail tip and gradient coloring from coat to flame red along the tail. Then I'm sketching a gold collar ring around the neck base with a pendant and tassels hanging off it.

Simplifying the collar to a single gold ring at radius 0.15, skipping the pendant and tassels for now, and noting hoof coloring and belly cream tone. I'm structuring the code with ring item types and a closed catmull-rom spline for the overall shape.

Now I'm working out hoof geometry—tapered cylinders wider at bottom than top, positioned with offset pairs at each foot to sit just above ground level, making sure they overlap cleanly with the leg sweep's end cap.

I'm also double-checking my imports to avoid unused ones, keeping only the utilities I actually reference like frame, rng, catmull, limb, countershade, gradient, scales, and the cel shading function. I'm applying a gradient between the coat color and hoof gold, wrapped in the cel shading helper for lit and shadow tones.

Now I'm sketching the flame SVG shape as two overlapping paths—an outer red-orange flame and an inner yellow-orange highlight—sized to a 40x100 viewbox, and setting up cloud SVG variants with different fill colors.
